run.rulesInOwnWords: 1) Input: add the cycle's row of inputs to each stage; no cap here. 2) Shunt: go stage 1 to 6 in order; if a stage is above its rated charge, cut it to rated and push the excess into the next stage (stage 6 excess goes to ground). Because it is sequential, pushed excess can cascade down within the same step. 3) Comparator (hysteresis): CLEAR becomes ASSERTED if charge >= upper mark; ASSERTED becomes CLEAR if charge <= lower mark; anything else keeps its state. Log each change. 4) Discharge: from the post-step-2 charges and post-step-3 states, compute all amounts first (CLEAR = floor(charge/4), ASSERTED = floor(charge/2)), then apply simultaneously: subtract from each stage; CLEAR amounts go to ground; ASSERTED amounts go back to stage n-1 (stage 1 ASSERTED goes to ground). No cap, so a stage can sit above rated until the next cycle's shunt. 5) Breaker: if total charge strictly > 38, every stage becomes floor(charge/2) and the removed charge goes to ground; log the trip. Exactly 38 does not trip. Repeat for cycles 1 to 5 and stop after step 5 of cycle 5.
run.balanceCheck: Starting charges 20 + inputs 94 = 114; end charges 38 + ground total 76 = 114. The two sides are equal.
run.notes: I used a Python script for the arithmetic and checked cycle 1 by hand. In cycle 5 the total is exactly 38, so the breaker does not trip (it trips only above 38). The cycle 5 return-diode feedback leaves stage 2 at 10 (rated 8) and stage 4 at 7 (rated 6). The procedure says to leave that excess in the end figures, so it is not shunted.
